newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: TRANSAVIA FACES MULTI-MILLION LOSS IN 96/97.
newsitem.headline: TRANSAVIA FACES MULTI-MILLION LOSS IN 96/97.

text.p: KLM's charter subsidiary Transavia said on Wednesday it was planning a cost-cutting drive to avoid ending its 1996/97 fiscal year with multi-million guilder losses.
"We are facing losses of several million guilders unless action is taken," Transavia spokesman Han Tonnen said.
He said the airline's chief executive officer Pieter Legro had written a letter to staff asking them to suggest ways of cutting costs and boosting revenues.
In addition Transavia had employed an external consultancy to review performance on various routes, Tonnen said.
But he added it was too early to say whether this would lead to certain routes being dropped.
Transavia has been badly hit by a severe downturn in holiday bookings, increased airline competition and rising fuel prices.
"Because holidays are our core business we are more exposed to the vagaries of the airline market than others," Tonnen said.
Transavia, which is 80 percent-owned by KLM, reported operating profit plunged 71 percent to 4.52 million guilders in the 1995/96 year ended March 31.
CEO Pieter Legro said then the airline would do its best to maintain its profitable run, unbroken since 1978.
